_comment: One vocabulary for the console and any future admin surface. Plain words a new reviewer can act on, not definitions of our internal names.

terms.plain: What the amounts on the panel are per: one capsule, two capsules, a scoop. Copy it exactly as printed. If the panel says 'per 2 capsules', the doses are for two, not one.
A row that shows only a percentage and no weight. Record the percentage and leave the amount blank. Do not calculate the milligrams yourself.

A named mixture with one total weight and its parts listed underneath. Record the blend as the parent and each part beneath it. The parts usually have no individual dose, and that blank is the correct answer.
Counts of live organisms in probiotics, not weights. Copy the unit exactly as printed; they are not interchangeable and neither is milligrams.
Whether the label lists non-active ingredients, says there are none, or folds them into the Facts panel. 'Not verified' is not a finding, it means nobody has looked yet.
Same barcode does not mean same product. A reformulation or a new size is a different label. Only mark duplicate when the printed label matches the one already in the catalog.

Use it instead of rejecting when the product is right but a panel is blurry, cut off or missing. Tick only the panels you need; the submitter keeps their other photos, the submission stays yours to review, and the new photos arrive as a new evidence revision.
The product is off the market. It still gets an accurate record; discontinued is a status, not a reason to reject.
How sure the model was about its own reading. It is a hint about where to look first. It is never evidence, and it can be confidently wrong.

rejections.use_when: You can tell what the product is but cannot read the panel.
One of the required faces was never photographed.
The panel is present but genuinely illegible. An unfamiliar language is not an unreadable photo: leave it for a reviewer who can verify that language.
The barcode, front and panel are not the same product.
Food, cosmetic, medicine, or anything outside the catalog.

after_approve: The label enters the next catalog build. It is scored by the pipeline, not by you or by the model, and the submitter is told their product is live once it ships.
